identity.title: Multiple Gaps in the Disk of the Class I Protostar GY 91

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present the highest spatial resolution ALMA observations to date of the Class I protostar GY 91 in the $\rho$ Ophiuchus L1688 molecular cloud complex.

evidence.quote: GY 91 is a M4 protostar (cite: Doppmann2005) in the L1688 region of the $\rho$ Ophiuchus molecular cloud, located at a distance of 137 pc (cite: OrtizLeon2017).
GY 91 is a M4 protostar (cite: Doppmann2005) in the L1688 region of the $\rho$ Ophiuchus molecular cloud, located at a distance of 137 pc (cite: OrtizLeon2017).

question.value: Does the Class I protostar GY 91 host gaps in its disk, are they similar to HL Tau's, and how young is it compared to HL Tau?

evidence.quote: We model these features assuming they are gaps in the disk surface density profile and find that their widths are 7 AU, 30 AU, and 10 AU.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2015.1.00761.S.
GY 91 was observed with ALMA Band 3 (100 GHz/3 mm) in three tracks from 31 October 2015 to 17 April 2016

analysis_steps.goal: Radiative transfer disk+envelope fit with gaps

method.value: Synthetic visibilities and SEDs fit simultaneously to 870 um, 3 mm and SED; gaps as multiplicative reductions of surface density

evidence.quote: We fit these synthetic observations simultaneously to all three (870 $\mu$m visibilities, 3 mm visibilities, and broadband SED) of our datasets, again using the `emcee` code.

assumptions.value: Lynden-Bell & Pringle surface density, Ulrich envelope, 10% uncertainty on literature photometry and IRS points

evidence.quote: we assume a constant 10% uncertainty on any photometry from the literature

fitting.value: emcee; median of walkers after burn-in, 68% range as uncertainty

evidence.quote: We estimate the uncertainty on these parameter values as the range around the median containing 68% of the walkers.

validation.value: Convergence judged by steady state of walkers

evidence.quote: We consider the fit to have converged when the walkers have reached a steady state

findings_qualitative.value: The outermost gap roughly matches the N2 freeze-out region; no snow line counterparts for the inner two gaps

evidence.quote: The outermost gap does roughly match the freeze out region of $N_2$. However no obvious counterparts are seen for the inner two gaps.

claims.experiment: 870 um and 3 mm imaging plus visibility modeling
claims.result: Three gaps at ~10, 41, 69 AU with widths 7, 30, 10 AU
claims.finding: Disk has three dark lanes resembling HL Tau

evidence.quote: the disk has three dark lanes located at 10 AU, 40 AU, and 70 AU.

claims.hypothesis: GY 91 is embedded and similar in age to HL Tau
claims.experiment: Same disk+envelope fit to both sources

evidence.quote: we also model the disk and envelope of HL Tau and find that they are of similar ages, although GY 91 may be younger.

claims.experiment: Gap width to planet mass relation
claims.finding: Saturn-mass planets possible, but snow lines and dead zones are alternatives

evidence.quote: Although snow lines and magnetic dead zones can also produce dark lanes

why_this_method.value: Geometric fit first because full radiative transfer is computationally expensive

evidence.quote: Because full radiative transfer modeling is very computationally intensive, we make initial estimates

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Snow lines/sintering and zonal flows as alternative gap origins

evidence.quote: Planets aren’t the only possible cause of these features.

limitations_admitted.value: Inner and outer gap depths not well constrained; planet mass estimates are crude without gas information

evidence.quote: The gap depths for the inner and outer gaps are not well constrained because they are not resolved well by our observations.
